title: Nan Cafe + Old Town: 2-Day Itinerary 2026 | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: A relaxed 2-day plan for Nan, Thailand: visit Wat Phumin and the old town in the morning, then hop between local coffee shops in the afternoon. With times, real cafes and rough prices.
keywords: Nan itinerary, Nan cafes, Nan old town, Wat Phumin, Nan walking street
intro: In Nan you can easily spend the morning visiting old temples and the afternoon lingering over coffee, because the main temples and the good cafes are clustered in the old town, almost all within walking distance of each other. This is a 2-day plan built so you barely break a sweat, getting both the old-town feel and locally grown Nan coffee.

blocks.html: The nice thing about Nan is how compact the old town is. Wat Phumin, the National Museum and Wat Phra That Chang Kham all sit inside the same small square, and you can loop around them on foot or by bicycle in just a few minutes. The cafes, meanwhile, line the streets of the Nai Wiang neighborhood all around. So this plan pairs the two: walk the old town in the morning while the sun is still gentle, duck into coffee shops in the afternoon, and head out to the walking street in the evening (Friday to Sunday only).

blocks.title: Before you set out
blocks.html: The Kad Khuang Mueang Nan walking street only runs on Friday, Saturday and Sunday evenings, so if you want to catch it, build your trip around a weekend. Many cafes also close early, around 5–6 PM, so if coffee is your priority, start hopping between shops in the early afternoon.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Walk the old town, morning to night

items.note: Nan's signature temple, home to the only cross-shaped ordination hall in Thailand. Step inside to see the 'Pu Man Ya Man' mural — the famous 'whispering of love' painting everyone photographs. Free entry. Go early while the crowds are thin and the light is good.

items.activity: Walk over to Wat Phra That Chang Kham
items.note: Right across from Wat Phumin, just a few steps away. A Sukhothai-style stupa ringed by elephant figures at its base — one of the old temples that has anchored the town for centuries.

Housed in the former royal palace hall, with the priceless 'Black Elephant Tusk' as its highlight. Out front is the frangipani-tree archway, a hugely popular photo spot. Entry is around 30 THB for Thai visitors. Closed Mondays and Tuesdays, so check the day before you go.
Find a spot for khanom jeen nam ngiao or khao soi around Nai Wiang. Northern dishes run about 40–60 THB a plate, and it's a short walk from the temple area.
A cafe in the Nai Wiang neighborhood that roasts its own 100% arabica beans. Easygoing atmosphere, coffee under 100 THB a cup — a good place to rest after a morning of temples.
A minimalist cafe in white-and-wood tones over in the Pha Sing area of Nai Wiang, with plenty of photo corners. Drinks 100–200 THB. Good for photos and long, slow conversations.

items.activity: Evening — Kad Khuang Mueang walking street (Fri–Sun)
items.note: Set up in front of Wat Phumin, it runs on Friday, Saturday and Sunday evenings, with local food, souvenirs, woven textiles and khantoke meals to eat roadside. If you land on a weeknight with no market, look for a northern restaurant in town instead.

blocks.text: Day 2 — A Full Day of Cafe-Hopping

items.activity: Start the morning at Erabica Coffee Nan
items.note: A roastery in a European-style building on Rangsi Kasem Road, serious about its coffee. Drinks 101–250 THB. Great if you're into tasting single-origin beans and espresso.
A cafe set in an old wooden house in Nai Wiang with a vintage feel and several coffees to choose from. Under 100 THB a cup, quiet and comfortable to sit in.

Stop by Comla Bakery & Baking Studio in Nai Wiang, which has a rotating selection of baked goods and occasionally runs baking workshops. Drinks and bakery items 100–250 THB. Or just grab lunch at a spot in town.
A Nai Wiang spot known for its 'coconut cake' at a friendly price under 100 THB — perfect for an afternoon dessert.

items.activity: Wind down with a walk along the Nan River
items.note: Stroll off your coffee along the Nan River in the softer late-afternoon light, snapping photos of the bridge and the town view. An easy way to close out the trip before you pack up.

blocks.text: Cafes in Nan worth choosing from

items.name: N. Nan Café
items.blurb: A cafe in the Nai Wiang neighborhood that roasts its own 100% arabica beans. Easygoing atmosphere and walkable from the temple area — a good first stop of the day.

items.name: Inlamai Coffee
items.blurb: A minimalist cafe in white-and-wood tones in the Pha Sing area, with lots of photo corners and some healthy-leaning menu options. Good for lingering chats and photos.

items.name: Erabica Coffee Nan
items.blurb: A roastery in a European-style building, serious about its beans and extraction. Great if you're into tasting espresso and black coffee.

items.name: Kaomai Nan
items.blurb: A cafe in an old wooden house with a vintage feel and several coffees to choose from. Quiet and comfortable, good for a rest.

items.name: Hugnan Baked Cafe
items.blurb: A spot known for its coconut cake at friendly prices — good for an afternoon dessert stop.

items.name: Comla Bakery & Baking Studio
items.blurb: A bakery with a rotating lineup of baked goods that occasionally runs baking classes. Good for bakery fans who want to try making their own.

blocks.title: Tips for walking the old town
blocks.html: Wat Phumin, the museum and Wat Phra That Chang Kham all sit in the same small square, so it's an easy loop on foot. Many hotels in town lend out bicycles, and cycling around the old town in the cool of the morning or evening is comfortable — and easier than driving when you want to stop at cafes.

items: Pick your day — if you want the walking street, stay over on a Friday or Saturday night, since the market only runs Friday to Sunday evenings.
Where to stay — choose a hotel in the Nai Wiang district and you'll be within walking distance of nearly all the temples and cafes, with no need to drive much.
Cafe hours — many shops close around 5–6 PM, so if you want to hit several, start in the early afternoon.
Leave room for the museum — the Nan National Museum is usually closed Mondays and Tuesdays, so check before planning Day 1.

faq.q: How many days do you need for cafes and the old town in Nan?
faq.a: Two days is about right. Spend the first day walking the old town (Wat Phumin, the museum, Wat Phra That Chang Kham) and dropping into cafes in the afternoon, then give the second day fully to cafe-hopping, since the temples and cafes are clustered in the Nai Wiang district and nearly all within walking distance.

faq.q: What days is the Nan walking street open?
faq.a: The Kad Khuang Mueang Nan walking street in front of Wat Phumin runs on Friday, Saturday and Sunday evenings. If you want to walk it, plan your trip around a weekend.

faq.q: Are the cafes in Nan walkable, or do you need to drive?
faq.a: Many of the cafes are in the Nai Wiang neighborhood around the old town, easily reached on foot or by bicycle, and several hotels lend out bikes. A few spots like Erabica are a little outside the temple area, so driving or grabbing a ride may be more convenient.

faq.q: Is there an entry fee for Wat Phumin and the museum?
faq.a: Wat Phumin is free to enter. The Nan National Museum charges around 30 THB for Thai visitors and is usually closed Mondays and Tuesdays, so check the opening days before you go.

faq.q: How much does coffee cost in Nan?
faq.a: Most cups run under 100 THB at wooden-house cafes and smaller shops, while roasteries and minimalist cafes are around 100–250 THB, depending on the drink and size.
